context.title: The Hour Has Come
context.summary: Mary anoints Jesus' feet at Bethany. Crowds with palm branches welcome him to Jerusalem. When Greeks ask to see him, Jesus says his hour has come and speaks of a grain of wheat that must die. Many still do not believe.
context.background: Palm branches were a symbol of victory and national hope; Jewish crowds had used them to celebrate the Maccabees' triumph (1 Maccabees 13:51). Until now Jesus has said 'mine hour is not yet come' (2:4); the arrival of Greeks marks the turn (v. 23).

customs.note: Costly perfume imported from the Himalayan region. Three hundred pence (denarii) was close to a year's wages.

watchFor: 'Except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die…' (v. 24).
'Now is my soul troubled' (v. 27), John's echo of Gethsemane.
John quotes Isaiah twice to explain unbelief (vv. 38–40).

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Lazarus
people.summary: The brother of Mary and Martha of Bethany. He was raised from the dead after he had lain four days in the tomb (John 11:1-44).

people.name: Martha
people.summary: Bitterness, the sister of Lazarus and Mary, and probably the eldest of the family, who all resided at Bethany (Luke 10:38, 40, 41; John 11:1-39).

people.name: Mary
people.summary: Mary the sister of Lazarus is brought to our notice in connection with the visits of our Lord to Bethany. She is contrasted with her sister Martha, who was “cumbered about many things” while Jesus was their guest, while Mary had chosen “the good part.”

people.name: Judas
people.summary: Son of Simon (John 6:71; 13:2, 26), surnamed Iscariot, i.e., a man of Kerioth (Josh. 15:25). His name is uniformly the last in the list of the apostles, as given in the synoptic (i.e., the first three) Gospels.

people.name: Philip
people.summary: One of the twelve apostles; a native of Bethsaida, “the city of Andrew and Peter” (John 1:44). He readily responded to the call of Jesus when first addressed to him (43), and forthwith brought Nathanael also to Jesus (45, 46).

people.name: Andrew
people.summary: Manliness, a Greek name; one of the apostles of our Lord. He was of Bethsaida in Galilee (John 1:44), and was the brother of Simon Peter (Matt. 4:18; 10:2).

people.name: Isaiah
people.summary: The son of Amoz (Isa. 1:1; 2:1), who was apparently a man of humble rank. His wife was called “the prophetess” (8:3), either because she was endowed with the prophetic gift, like Deborah (Judg. 4:4) and Huldah (2 Kings 22:14-20), or simply because she was the wife of “the prophet” (Isa. 38:1).

places.name: Bethany
places.summary: A village on the south-eastern slope of the Mount of Olives (Mark 11:1), about 2 miles east of Jerusalem, on the road to Jericho. It derived its name from the number of palm-trees which grew there.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Zion
places.summary: Sunny; height, one of the eminences on which Jerusalem was built. It was surrounded on all sides, except the north, by deep valleys, that of the Tyropoeon separating it from Moriah, which it surpasses in height by 105 feet.

places.name: Bethsaida
places.summary: A city near which Christ fed 5,000 (Luke 9:10; comp. John 6:17; Matt. 14:15-21), and where the blind man had his sight restored (Mark 8:22), on the east side of the lake, two miles up the Jordan.

places.name: Galilee
places.summary: Circuit. Solomon rewarded Hiram for certain services rendered him by the gift of an upland plain among the mountains of Naphtali. Hiram was dissatisfied with the gift, and called it “the land of Cabul”.

events.title: Mary Anoints Jesus
events.summary: Passage: John 12:1–11. People: Jesus, Mary, Martha, Lazarus. Place: Bethany.

events.title: Holy Week
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 21:1 – John 20:31. Place: Jerusalem. Lasted about 8 days.

events.title: Triumphal Entry
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 21:1 – John 12:19. People: Jesus. Place: Jerusalem.
